newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Sao Paulo bourse to implement new custody system.
newsitem.headline: Sao Paulo bourse to implement new custody system.

text.p: Brazil's Sao Paulo Stock Exchange (Bovespa), South America's largest bourse, said it will begin operating March 3 a new on-line custody system for storing and safekeeping shares.
The new "real-time" system will be designed to improve efficiency and security for brokerages and investors at the time they go to store securities, the bourse said in a statement.
The planned system was unveiled Tuesday by Bovespa President Alfredo Rizkallah at a meeting with brokerage officials, it said.
The new system "involves the most advanced information technology and represents indispensible security for the marketing of shares in the capital markets," he was quoted as saying.
The statement also said the bolsa plans to fuse its live-voice and CATS trading systems into a single system, known as MEGA BOLSA, by the end of the year.
The move will make the Sao Paulo bourse compatible with world markets now undergoing rapid globalization, it added.
